# Agent Instructions

All agent-facing instructions live in this file. `CLAUDE.md` contains only a
reference here. If you are a Claude Code agent, you have already loaded this
via `CLAUDE.md`. Other agents: read this file directly.

## Build and test

```bash
# Run unit tests (REQUIRED before every PR)
pip install pytest  # if not already installed
python3 -m pytest tests/ -v

# Validate imports
python3 -c "from runner import main"
python3 -c "from generate_results import generate_results_md"
python3 -c "from test_quality import compute_structural_metrics"
python3 -c "from llm_providers import get_provider"
python3 -c "from version_docs import build_doc, main"
python3 -c "from combine_results import combine"

# Regenerate all reports
python3 generate_results.py --all

# Run a benchmark (v4, all tasks/modes/models). Use 5 modes including
# powershell-tool. For multi-(model,effort) matrices, run sequentially via
# a wrapper script (see run-fresh-matrix-2026-05-06.sh).
python3 runner.py --tasks 11,12,13,15,16,17,18 --modes default,powershell,powershell-tool,bash,typescript-bun --models opus,sonnet

# Watch a run while it is still in progress (read-only live dashboard). Reads
# whatever metrics.json files exist so far; never touches the run. The head-to-head
# is automatic: the strongest model+version in this run vs the strongest in the
# previous report (newest completed run), broken down per scripting language.
# Override the auto-pick with --baseline DIR and/or --pair RUNVAR=BASEVAR.
python3 monitor.py --total 140 --watch 30                 # newest run, refresh 30s

# Build per-CC-version reference docs in each run dir (system prompt +
# tool descriptions + sliced changelog). Idempotent; caches under
# .cache/cc-versions/.
python3 version_docs.py                   # all run dirs
python3 version_docs.py results/<run-dir> # one run

# Evaluate test quality (structural metrics only)
python3 test_quality.py results/2026-04-09_152435

# Evaluate test + deliverable quality with the default panel of judges
# (Haiku 4.5 via claude-cli + Gemini 3.1 Pro via the agy CLI). Each judge
# writes its own cache file: test-quality-{short}.json and
# deliverable-quality-{short}.json. 8-worker thread pool by default;
# bump `--workers` if your CLIs + account limits allow more concurrency.
python3 test_quality.py --llm-judge --deliverable-judge \
    --judges haiku45,gemini31pro --workers 8 results/2026-04-17_004319

# Re-evaluate with a single judge only (useful for bias cross-checks)
python3 test_quality.py --llm-judge --judges haiku45 results/2026-04-17_004319

# Build custom act container (optional, eliminates pwsh install overhead)
docker build -t act-ubuntu-pwsh:latest -f Dockerfile.act .
```

## Code style

- Python 3.12+. No type stubs or mypy. Use type hints where they aid readability.
- Dollar amounts in results.md: round to nearest penny (`.2f`).
- Durations in results.md: always in minutes with 1 decimal (`{seconds/60:.1f}min`).
- No emojis in code or docs unless the user asks.

## Terminology

When the runtime wrapper uses `language_mode` (Python-side variable name), the
*user-facing* axis is called **language**, never "mode". This covers docs,
prompts, report prose, and LLM summaries. The internal field name stays
`language_mode` so existing metrics.json readers don't break; everything else
says "language" (e.g. "default/Python, bash, powershell, powershell-tool,
typescript-bun"). Rationale: "mode" is ambiguous with agent-approval-modes and
execution modes; "language" is the concept readers expect.

## Repository rules

- **No agent-generated `.github/workflows/` at repo root.** Agent workflows only exist inside workspaces under `workspaces/`. The repo's own CI workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) is the exception.
- **Never fix agent-generated code.** The benchmark measures autonomous output. Do not manually fix, edit, or patch workflow files in `workspaces/` or `results/*/generated-code/`.
- **`runner.py` observes and records, never intervenes** on agent code or errors.
- **Always set effort and context explicitly — never omit them and rely on CLI defaults.** Every benchmark invocation must pass `--effort <level>` (for models that support effort) and choose the context window explicitly (via the model id, using the `[1m]` suffix when 1M is intended). The Claude Code CLI's *default* effort level and *default* context window are **model- and CLI-version-dependent** and are **not** captured in `metrics.json` or the CLI's JSON response. So a cell run without them cannot be labeled with certainty afterward — you can only infer the effort/context from whatever the docs say *now*, which may not match the CLI version that actually ran. Omitting them forfeits reproducibility and forces after-the-fact assumptions in reports. (Only exception: models that reject `--effort`, e.g. Haiku 4.5 — there is no effort to pin; record that fact in the variant label, e.g. `-na` for "not applicable".) Effort especially, then context, must be pinned on every run.
- **Standard language set is four; `powershell-tool` is dropped.** Run `default,powershell,bash,typescript-bun`. `powershell-tool` is functionally identical to `powershell` when act runs under WSL (same pwsh, same behavior), so it only duplicates the PowerShell data — do not run it.
- **Post a live status heartbeat during benchmark runs.** While a benchmark is collecting, relay the full `monitor.py --total <expected-cells>` report to the user roughly every 30 minutes — it includes the completion-time ETA, the per-variant summary, the head-to-head same-task comparison against the strongest prior model, and the per-language breakdown. Monitor-tool events are agent-facing and do **not** reach the user's chat on their own, so post the output in a message (a persistent Monitor is a convenient 30-minute trigger). This is the default whenever the user asks for a benchmark run.
- **Workspaces are throwaway.** Don't commit `workspaces/` contents.
- **`results/` is committed.** It contains archived metrics, generated code, and transcripts.
- **`CLAUDE.md` is only a pointer.** All instructions go in `AGENTS.md`. Never put substantive content in `CLAUDE.md` — it should only reference this file.

## Architecture

### Key files

- `models.py` — single source of truth for model IDs and token pricing. Update here when Anthropic changes prices.
- `runner.py` — benchmark harness. Runs agents via `claude -p`, collects metrics, pushes results. Imports from `models.py` and `generate_results.py`. Robustness invariants added 2026-06:
  - **Single-runner lock.** On startup it takes an exclusive non-blocking `flock` on `<repo>/.runner.lock` (`acquire_single_runner_lock`); a second runner exits(2) rather than execute cells concurrently — concurrent cells compete for CPU/Docker/pwsh and confound each other's timing/cost. (Released automatically on exit.)
  - **Resume validity.** `--resume` skips a cell only when its `metrics.json` is non-empty + parseable (`_metrics_valid`), so a write interrupted by a crash/teardown is re-run rather than skipped forever, leaving a hole.
  - **Honest push logging + commit-per-cell.** The `PeriodicPusher` thread commits+pushes `results/` **once per newly-completed cell** (wakes every `PUSH_CHECK_INTERVAL`s, commits only when `run_count` increased) — one commit per result, each pushed immediately. `git_push_results` checks the push exit code and logs an explicit WARNING on failure instead of always printing "Pushed results".
- `generate_results.py` — generates `results.md` reports and updates `README.md`. Can run standalone: `python3 generate_results.py --all`. Each results.md opens with a "Claude Code versions used" line linking to the per-version docs (see `version_docs.py`).
- `combine_results.py` — produces cross-run combined reports `results/results_<dirA>__<dirB>[__<dirC>...].md`. Same table layout as per-run reports plus a CLI Version Legend; uses `judge_consistency_report.py` for the JCS section and `conclusions_report.py` for the Opus-max Conclusions prose. Standalone: `python3 combine_results.py <dirA> <dirB> [<dirC> ...]`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# cleanup-artifacts.sh
#
# Manages GitHub Actions artifact cleanup based on retention policies.
# Operates on a mock JSON fixture of artifacts (no real GitHub API calls).
#
# Policies (all optional, combinable):
#   --max-age-days N        delete artifacts older than N days
#   --max-total-size N      delete oldest artifacts until total size <= N bytes
#   --keep-latest N         always keep the N most recent artifacts per workflow
#   --dry-run               only print the plan, do not "delete" (mock deletion)
#   --now EPOCH             override "current time" (epoch seconds) - for testing
#   --fixture FILE          path to JSON artifact fixture (required)
#
# Fixture format: JSON array of objects, each with:
#   name (string), size_bytes (number), created_at (ISO8601 UTC, e.g.
#   "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"), workflow (string), run_id (number/string)
#
# Combined-policy algorithm:
#   1. Compute the "protected" set: for each workflow, the N most recent
#      artifacts (by created_at) are protected by --keep-latest and are never
#      deleted, regardless of age or size.
#   2. Among non-protected artifacts, any older than --max-age-days is marked
#      for deletion (age deletion).
#   3. Among the artifacts that survive steps 1-2 (protected + age-survivors),
#      if their total size exceeds --max-total-size, the non-protected
#      age-survivors are deleted oldest-first until the total size is under
#      the cap (size deletion).
#   4. Everything not deleted in steps 2-3 is retained.
#
# This file is safe to `source` for unit testing individual functions; the
# CLI entrypoint only runs when the script is executed directly.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_NAME="$(basename "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"

err() {
  echo "Error: $*" >&2
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Validation / parsing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# validate_and_load_fixture FILE
# Prints the parsed JSON array (validated) on stdout, or errors out.
validate_and_load_fixture() {
  local file="$1"

  if [[ -z "$file" ]]; then
    err "No fixture file specified (use --fixture FILE)"
    return 2
  fi

  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then
    err "Fixture file not found: $file"
    return 2
  fi

  if ! jq empty "$file" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    err "Invalid JSON in fixture file: $file"
    return 3
  fi

  local valid
  valid=$(jq -e '
    type == "array" and
    all(.[]; (has("name") and has("size_bytes") and has("created_at") and has("workflow")))
  ' "$file" 2>/dev/null) || valid="false"

  if [[ "$valid" != "true" ]]; then
    err "Fixture file is missing required fields (name, size_bytes, created_at, workflow): $file"
    return 3
  fi

  jq -c '.' "$file"
}

# is_valid_uint VALUE
is_valid_uint() {
  [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Individual policy filters (each returns {"retained": [...], "deleted": [...]})
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# filter_by_age ARTIFACTS_JSON MAX_AGE_DAYS NOW_EPOCH
filter_by_age() {
  local artifacts="$1" max_age_days="$2" now="$3"
  jq -c --argjson now "$now" --argjson max_age_days "$max_age_days" '
    def age_days: ($now - (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)) / 86400;
    {
      deleted: [.[] | select(age_days > $max_age_days)],
      retained: [.[] | select(age_days <= $max_age_days)]
    }
  ' <<<"$artifacts"
}

# filter_by_size ARTIFACTS_JSON MAX_TOTAL_SIZE
# Sorts oldest-first and deletes until total size <= cap.
filter_by_size() {
  local artifacts="$1" max_total_size="$2"
  jq -c --argjson cap "$max_total_size" '
    (sort_by(.created_at | fromdateiso8601)) as $sorted |
    reduce $sorted[] as $a
      ({running: ([$sorted[] | .size_bytes] | add // 0), deleted: [], retained: []};
        if .running > $cap then
          {running: (.running - $a.size_bytes), deleted: (.deleted + [$a]), retained: .retained}
        else
          {running: .running, deleted: .deleted, retained: (.retained + [$a])}
        end
      ) | {deleted, retained}
  ' <<<"$artifacts"
}

# filter_by_keep_latest ARTIFACTS_JSON KEEP_N
# "retained" = protected (N most recent per workflow); "deleted" = the rest.
filter_by_keep_latest() {
  local artifacts="$1" keep_n="$2"
  jq -c --argjson n "$keep_n" '
    group_by(.workflow) |
    map(sort_by(.created_at | fromdateiso8601) | reverse) |
    map({protected: .[0:$n], rest: .[$n:]}) as $groups |
    {
      retained: [$groups[].protected] | add // [],
      deleted: [$groups[].rest] | add // []
    }
  ' <<<"$artifacts"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Combined policy application
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# apply_policies ARTIFACTS_JSON MAX_AGE_DAYS MAX_TOTAL_SIZE KEEP_N NOW_EPOCH
# MAX_AGE_DAYS / MAX_TOTAL_SIZE may be empty string to mean "no limit".
# KEEP_N may be empty string to mean "0" (no protection).
apply_policies() {
  local artifacts="$1" max_age_days="$2" max_total_size="$3" keep_n="$4" now="$5"

  local keep_n_eff="${keep_n:-0}"
  local protected retained_after_keep
  protected=$(filter_by_keep_latest "$artifacts" "$keep_n_eff")
  local protected_list candidates
  protected_list=$(jq -c '.retained' <<<"$protected")
  candidates=$(jq -c '.deleted' <<<"$protected")

  local age_deleted age_survivors
  if [[ -n "$max_age_days" ]]; then
    local age_result
    age_result=$(filter_by_age "$candidates" "$max_age_days" "$now")
    age_deleted=$(jq -c '.deleted' <<<"$age_result")
    age_survivors=$(jq -c '.retained' <<<"$age_result")
  else
    age_deleted='[]'
    age_survivors="$candidates"
  fi

  local size_deleted size_survivors
  if [[ -n "$max_total_size" ]]; then
    # Total size to consider = protected + age_survivors combined.
    local combined
    combined=$(jq -c -s 'add' <<<"$protected_list"$'\n'"$age_survivors")
    local size_result
    size_result=$(jq -c --argjson protcount "$(jq 'length' <<<"$protected_list")" '
      .
    ' <<<"$combined" >/dev/null; filter_by_size "$combined" "$max_total_size")
    # size_result classifies protected + age_survivors together; we must
    # never actually delete protected artifacts, so subtract them back out.
    size_deleted=$(jq -c --argjson prot "$protected_list" '
      .deleted - $prot
    ' <<<"$size_result")
    size_survivors=$(jq -c --argjson prot "$protected_list" '
      .retained - $prot
    ' <<<"$size_result")
  else
    size_deleted='[]'
    size_survivors="$age_survivors"
  fi

  local all_deleted all_retained
  all_deleted=$(jq -c -s 'add' <<<"$age_deleted"$'\n'"$size_deleted")
  all_retained=$(jq -c -s 'add' <<<"$protected_list"$'\n'"$size_survivors")

  local deleted_count retained_count bytes_reclaimed
  deleted_count=$(jq 'length' <<<"$all_deleted")
  retained_count=$(jq 'length' <<<"$all_retained")
  bytes_reclaimed=$(jq '[.[] | .size_bytes] | add // 0' <<<"$all_deleted")

  jq -n -c \
    --argjson deleted "$all_deleted" \
    --argjson retained "$all_retained" \
    --argjson deleted_count "$deleted_count" \
    --argjson retained_count "$retained_count" \
    --argjson bytes_reclaimed "$bytes_reclaimed" \
    '{
      deleted: $deleted,
      retained: $retained,
      summary: {
        deleted_count: $deleted_count,
        retained_count: $retained_count,
        bytes_reclaimed: $bytes_reclaimed
      }
    }'
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plan / summary output
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# print_plan PLAN_JSON DRY_RUN(true|false)
print_plan() {
  local plan="$1" dry_run="$2"

  local deleted_count retained_count bytes_reclaimed
  deleted_count=$(jq -r '.summary.deleted_count' <<<"$plan")
  retained_count=$(jq -r '.summary.retained_count' <<<"$plan")
  bytes_reclaimed=$(jq -r '.summary.bytes_reclaimed' <<<"$plan")

  echo "Artifact Cleanup Plan"
  echo "====================="

  if [[ "$dry_run" == "true" ]]; then
    while IFS= read -r name; do
      echo "[DRY RUN] Would delete artifact: $name"
    done < <(jq -r '.deleted[].name' <<<"$plan")
  else
    while IFS= read -r name; do
      echo "Deleting artifact: $name"
    done < <(jq -r '.deleted[].name' <<<"$plan")
  fi

  while IFS= read -r name; do
    echo "Retaining artifact: $name"
  done < <(jq -r '.retained[].name' <<<"$plan")

  echo "---------------------"
  echo "Summary:"
  echo "  Deleted:  $deleted_count"
  echo "  Retained: $retained_count"
  echo "  Bytes reclaimed: $bytes_reclaimed"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLI entrypoint
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $SCRIPT_NAME --fixture FILE [options]

Options:
  --fixture FILE          Path to JSON artifact fixture (required)
  --max-age-days N        Delete artifacts older than N days
  --max-total-size N      Delete oldest artifacts until total size <= N bytes
  --keep-latest N         Always keep the N most recent artifacts per workflow
  --dry-run               Only print the plan, do not "delete" anything
  --now EPOCH             Override current time (epoch seconds), for testing
  -h, --help              Show this help
EOF
}

main() {
  local fixture="" max_age_days="" max_total_size="" keep_latest="" dry_run="false"
  local now
  now=$(date -u +%s)

  while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
      --fixture)
        fixture="${2:-}"
        shift 2
        ;;
      --max-age-days)
        max_age_days="${2:-}"
        if ! is_valid_uint "$max_age_days"; then
          err "--max-age-days requires a non-negative integer, got: '$max_age_days'"
          exit 4
        fi
        shift 2

2	#
3	# artifact-cleanup.sh
4	#
5	# Computes a GitHub Actions artifact deletion plan against a local JSON
6	# fixture file (no real GitHub API calls are ever made). Supports three
7	# retention policies that can be combined:
8	#   --max-age-days N        delete artifacts older than N days
9	#   --max-total-size-bytes N delete oldest artifacts until under the cap
10	#   --keep-latest-n N       always keep the N most recent artifacts per
11	#                            workflow (workflow_name), regardless of the
12	#                            other two policies
13	#
14	# Policy combination order (documented design decision):
15	#   1. keep-latest-N artifacts per workflow are "protected" and are never
16	#      candidates for deletion by any other policy.
17	#   2. Among the remaining (unprotected) artifacts, the age policy marks
18	#      artifacts older than the cutoff for deletion.
19	#   3. Among the artifacts still remaining (unprotected and not already
20	#      marked for deletion by the age policy), the size policy deletes the
21	#      oldest artifacts first until the total size of what remains is at or
22	#      under the cap.
23	#
24	# Exit codes:
25	#   0  success
26	#   2  fixture file not found
27	#   3  invalid JSON / invalid fixture structure
28	#   4  invalid numeric flag value
29	#   5  unknown flag
30	#   6  missing required argument (e.g. --fixture)

42	  --max-age-days N              Delete artifacts older than N days
43	  --max-total-size-bytes N      Delete oldest artifacts until total size <= N
44	  --keep-latest-n N              Keep N most recent artifacts per workflow
45	  --dry-run                     Only print the plan; perform no deletion
46	  --now TIMESTAMP                Override "current time" (ISO 8601, for tests)
47	  -h, --help                    Show this help message

49	}

3	# run-act-harness.sh
4	#
5	# Runs `act push --rm` against the artifact-cleanup-script workflow, captures
6	# the full output, appends it to act-result.txt at the repo root, asserts
7	# act exited 0, and greps the captured output for exact expected values for
8	# each retention-policy scenario (counts deleted/retained, bytes reclaimed).
9	#
10	# Also runs the structural workflow checks (test/workflow_structure.bats)
11	# and records their result.
12	#
13	# NOTE: invoking this harness consumes one of the task's limited `act push`
14	# invocations.
15	
16	set -euo pipefail
17	
18	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
19	cd "${REPO_ROOT}"
20	
21	RESULT_FILE="${REPO_ROOT}/act-result.txt"
22	ACT_LOG="$(mktemp)"
23	trap 'rm -f "${ACT_LOG}"' EXIT
24	
25	echo "=== run-act-harness.sh started at $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) ===" | tee -a "${RESULT_FILE}"
26	
27	echo "--- Structural workflow checks (bats test/workflow_structure.bats) ---" | tee -a "${RESULT_FILE}"
28	if bats test/workflow_structure.bats 2>&1 | tee -a "${RESULT_FILE}"; then
29	  echo "STRUCTURAL CHECKS: PASS" | tee -a "${RESULT_FILE}"
30	else
31	  echo "STRUCTURAL CHECKS: FAIL" | tee -a "${RESULT_FILE}"
32	  exit 1
33	fi
34	
35	echo "--- actionlint on workflow file ---" | tee -a "${RESULT_FILE}"
36	if actionlint .github/workflows/artifact-cleanup-script.yml 2>&1 | tee -a "${RESULT_FILE}"; then
37	  echo "ACTIONLINT: PASS (exit 0)" | tee -a "${RESULT_FILE}"
38	else

40	  exit 1
41	fi
42

44	set +e
45	act push --rm >"${ACT_LOG}" 2>&1
46	ACT_STATUS=$?
47	set -e
48	
49	cat "${ACT_LOG}" >>"${RESULT_FILE}"
50	echo "=== act push --rm exited with status ${ACT_STATUS} ===" | tee -a "${RESULT_FILE}"
51
